statement: Parametric attaining theorem and matching delimited method barriers. If 9/23<theta<1 satisfies the source paper's short-prime count PI(theta), then for every fixed 0<c<(1-theta)/3 and all sufficiently large k, every integer 2k<n<=exp(c(log k)^2/loglog k) has a prime divisor p in (k,k+3k^theta) of (n-k)...(n-1), hence p in (k,2k). With the Baker--Harman--Pintz value theta=21/40, this gives every c<19/120. The explicitly defined balanced four-range parameter class is feasible exactly when 9/23<theta<1 and c<(1-theta)/3: its r=3 sharp additive exponent blocks theta<=9/23, while its first growing-order margin blocks theta>=1 for c>0. Independently, no termwise blockwise Theorem 4.1 little-o certificate as precisely defined in evidence/parametric_frontier_proof.md reaches c>=(1-theta)/3. Both no-go claims are confined to their stated certificate classes, not the true bad-point count or Erdős #451 as a whole.

dependency_gaps: The abstract theta theorem assumes PI(theta); the theta=21/40 corollary imports the Baker--Harman--Pintz short-prime input exactly as the source paper does.

The complete four-range ParametricRangeBuilder and final conditional theorem are kernel-checked in Lean on the widest window proved for this method, 9/23<theta<1. The sharp large-range additive estimate ((4-theta)r+theta-3)/(r(3r-2)) <= (9-2theta)/21 is absorbable exactly when theta>9/23; there is no remaining builder gap.
